reason: Equivalent: `if TYPE_CHECKING:` -> `if False:` skips the same block at run time, because typing.TYPE_CHECKING is False there, and the block holds only a type-checking import of open_meteo.SolarDiagnostics; under `from __future__ import annotations` nothing evaluates that name. Measured at 5c69edd8d against the mutant, under Python 3.13 with tests/requirements-ci.txt's versions: the imported module namespace (every name, and each TypedDict's annotations and required/optional keys) is byte-identical, where the control `if True:` adds SolarDiagnostics; the pinned ruler (`typing_ruler.py --mypy`, mypy 2.3.1, homeassistant-stubs 2026.9.3, Python 3.14) prints an identical report, where the control deleting the import gives name-defined +1; and every source-reading driver in payload.py's closure is green at both ends: harness_headers, entities, doc_claims, guard_pins, typing_ruler, validate, deployment_shape, finite_boundary, structure, arch_score_head, wood_advisor, manual_plan, plan_view, config_flow_steps, solar_alignment, edge. CI agrees: mutation jobs 111092950838 and 111092963010 report the site LIVES with every driver green. This replaces a killed_by pin to tests/harness_headers.py recorded against 16551007, before #1872 pinned BLAS threads in harness_headers' children; harness_headers passes 94 of 94 on the mutant. The `if not TYPE_CHECKING:` direction is killed by entities.py's `EG-B3b: payload.py loads with no package` check; this mutant is not that one.
